questions.text: A startup is building an LLM for a low resource agglutinative language where a single word can contain information equivalent to an entire English sentence. After training a Word Level tokenizer with a vocabulary of 30,000, they observe that nearly 18% of tokens become [UNK]. Which action is most likely to improve the situation while keeping vocabulary growth manageable?
options: Use SentencePiece or BPE
Increase batch size
Increase the minimum token frequency threshold during tokenizer training
Disable normalization so every word form is stored separately

questions.text: A team fine tunes a 13B parameter model using LoRA. After training they discover that only 0.15% of parameters have been updated. Which statement best explains this observation?
options: LoRA updates low rank matrices while freezing most pretrained weights
LoRA trains only the embedding layer
LoRA automatically quantizes the model
LoRA removes attention layers during training
questions.correct_answer: LoRA updates low rank matrices while freezing most pretrained weights

questions.text: A company wants to build a medical chatbot. They possess: • 8 million unlabeled medical documents • 300 doctor reviewed question answer pairs Which adaptation strategy would most likely provide the largest performance gain?
options: Train a new tokenizer only
Continue pretraining on the medical corpus and then instruction tune
Increase context length
Increase batch size
questions.correct_answer: Continue pretraining on the medical corpus and then instruction tune

questions.text: A tokenizer vocabulary is increased from 16K to 128K while keeping the training corpus unchanged. What tradeoff is most likely?
options: Shorter sequences and a larger embedding layer
Longer sequences and a smaller embedding layer
Shorter sequences and a smaller embedding layer
No significant effect on the model
questions.correct_answer: Shorter sequences and a larger embedding layer
